title: Model onboarding: license & restricted-weights compliance checks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add an automated compliance gate to the model-onboarding pipeline that validates licensing, redistribution restrictions, and presence of restricted/proprietary weights before a model can be published to the Redwood model catalog or used by Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. Gate must produce a machine-readable report, a human-readable summary for legal/PM review, and integrate with version pinning and performance-profile publishing flows. Goal: reduce legal review cycle time, prevent accidental onboarding of models with incompatible licenses or restricted third-party weights, and ensure all published profiles are tied to a pinned, verified model artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New 'license_and_weights_check' step added to onboarding pipeline that returns PASS/WARN/FAIL.
2) Automated license classifier executes on model metadata and file manifests and flags non-permissive licenses (e.g., CC-BY-NC, proprietary).
3) Binary/weight fingerprinting detects known restricted or third-party proprietary blobs via hash lookup and heuristics.
4) Models with FAIL cannot be published; WARN requires manual legal sign-off.
5) When PASS, pipeline attaches a signed artifact reference and the model can be version-pinned and have a performance profile published.
6) Generated report is stored in onboarding artifacts and surfaced in the Console model detail page.
7) Audit logs and event stream emit policy decisions for compliance reporting.
notes: Context: PM-4217 implemented automated model entry guard for metadata and provenance. This ticket extends the guard to include license interpretation and restricted weights detection. Legal review asked for human-readable rationale for WARN/FAIL cases and a secure way to store sign-offs for Private deployments. Targeting runtime-1.22 because this ties into Dedicated capacity rollout and auditability requirements for enterprise customers.

We saw one candidate model in staging flagged with a CC-BY-NC license; need to prevent it from being published to hosted customers. Link to Confluence brief: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Model+Onboarding+License+Gate

Two false positives were unusual dual-license headers (MIT + custom). We should add a heuristic to prefer the more restrictive license for safe default. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboard/pull/234

2026-02-20 — Legal (Priya Ramesh): We need: 1) list of blocked license terms, 2) escalation flow for WARN cases, 3) retention policy for sign-offs. Also require storing the exact model checksum and source URL for audit. I'll add the policy doc to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Compliance/ModelLicenses

2026-02-25 — Eng (Diego Torres): Dependency: ENG-5123 (build a centralized hash-index and offline scanner) must be complete before we can validate weight blobs at scale. We can wire the classifier into the onboarding runner as a step and fail fast for large models to avoid wasted compute. Estimate 3 sprint points for integration + UI surface in Console.

2026-03-03 — Marcus Li: Proposal for user flows: (A) For hosted catalog entries, FAIL prevents publish and notifies model owner with failure report. (B) For Private installs, allow an enterprise opt-in override but require a recorded legal sign-off and a clear audit entry. Wire this into RBAC and Private control plane. Logged design decision in doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/License+Gate+Decision

2026-03-08 — Legal (Priya Ramesh): Reviewed prototype reports. Request: include the exact license text snippet and the matched file path/URL. For weight fingerprint matches, include the matched hash and known attribution. Also ask for an allowlist/denylist UI for future updates.

2026-03-10 — UX (Lena Kim): Console addition: model detail panel should show: license status badge, link to detailed compliance report, last-signed-off-by, and sign-off history. We'll prototype in Figma and share next week. Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/ModelOnboardingCompliance

2026-03-12 — Marcus Li: Integration tests passing in staging. Current behavior: classifier returns PASS/WARN/FAIL; WARN creates a 'legal_review' task in Linear (PM/manual step). Next steps: add signed artifact storage (ENG-5199) and implement Console UI. Creating sub-issues to track follow-ups: PM-4382-1 (Console UI), PM-4382-2 (Sign-off storage), PM-4382-3 (Enterprise override flow).

Decision log: We will default to FAIL on ambiguous license metadata (safety-first). WARN will be a gated state that requires a legal sign-off recorded in the system before publishing. Enterprise override allowed only with recorded sign-off and an optional risk-acknowledgement document.
